section: Working with Pipelines in Developer perspective
job_statement: When I need to build CI/CD automation for my application, I want to create custom pipelines using the web console, so I can automate my software delivery process without writing YAML manually
prerequisites: OpenShift Pipelines Operator installed; Developer perspective access; Project/namespace access
desired_outcomes: Pipeline created and ready to execute; Tasks configured with proper dependencies; Resources and parameters defined; Pipeline appears in Pipelines view
evidence: Pipeline builder form; YAML view option; Task search and installation from Tekton Hub; Visual pipeline representation
notes: Core job for pipeline creation, covers both Pipeline builder UI and YAML editing approaches

job_statement: When I am building a pipeline, I want to search and add tasks from Tekton Hub or my cluster, so I can assemble pipelines from reusable components instead of writing tasks from scratch
prerequisites: Pipeline builder open; Tekton Hub accessible or cluster tasks available
desired_outcomes: Tasks added to pipeline; Task dependencies configured; Finally tasks added if needed; Tasks show Install/Add/Update status correctly
evidence: Quick search field for tasks; Add/Install and add/Update and add buttons; Visual task ordering with plus icons; Add finally task option
notes: Allows discovery and reuse of tasks, central to visual pipeline construction

job_statement: When I am defining my pipeline, I want to specify resources, parameters, and workspaces, so I can provide the inputs and outputs my pipeline tasks need to execute
prerequisites: Pipeline builder open; Tasks added to pipeline
desired_outcomes: Git and Image resources defined; Parameters configured for tasks; Workspaces created and assigned; Error indicators cleared
evidence: Add Resources section; Resource type dropdown (Git, Image); Add Parameters link; Add workspace section; Task side panel for resource assignment
notes: Critical for connecting pipelines to source code and container registries

job_statement: When I am deploying an application from Git, I want to automatically create a pipeline for it, so I can set up CI/CD as part of my initial application deployment
prerequisites: Developer perspective access; Git repository with application code
desired_outcomes: Application deployed; Pipeline created and associated with application; Webhook configured for Git events; Pipeline visible in Topology view
evidence: +Add -> From Git flow; Pipeline template selection; Automatic webhook creation; Topology view integration
notes: Streamlined workflow combining application deployment and pipeline creation

section: Adding a GitHub repository containing pipelines
job_statement: When I have pipelines defined in my GitHub repository, I want to connect my repository to the cluster, so I can run pipelines from Git events like pushes and pull requests
prerequisites: GitHub application configured by administrator; Public or private GitHub repository; Personal access token or token secret
desired_outcomes: Repository connected to cluster; Webhook configured in GitHub; Pipelines as Code enabled; Git events trigger pipeline runs
evidence: Create -> Repository flow; Git Repo URL input; GitHub App vs webhook options; Webhook URL and secret generation; Show configuration options
notes: Enables GitOps-style pipeline execution, supports both public and private repos

job_statement: When I am setting up webhook authentication, I want to use either a personal access token or a token secret, so I can securely authorize GitHub to trigger my pipelines
prerequisites: Repository creation flow open; GitHub personal access token or existing secret
desired_outcomes: Webhook secret generated; Authentication configured; Webhook details ready for GitHub configuration
evidence: Git access token field; Git access token secret dropdown; Generate button for webhook secret; Link to create new token
notes: Two authentication paths provide flexibility for different security requirements

section: Interacting with pipelines using Developer perspective
job_statement: When I need to understand my pipeline structure and status, I want to view pipeline details visually, so I can see task dependencies, execution status, and configuration at a glance
prerequisites: Pipeline exists in project; Pipelines view access
desired_outcomes: Pipeline visualization displayed; Task details accessible; Serial, parallel, and finally tasks visible; When expressions shown; Parameters and resources reviewable
evidence: Visual pipeline representation; Zoom controls; Task detail on hover; Details/Metrics/YAML/Pipeline Runs tabs; Tasks and Finally tasks lists
notes: Primary monitoring and understanding interface for pipelines

section: Interacting with pipelines using Developer perspective
job_statement: When I want to improve my pipeline performance, I want to see metrics about success rates, run counts, and durations, so I can identify bottlenecks and optimization opportunities
prerequisites: Pipeline with run history; Metrics tab available
desired_outcomes: Success ratio visible; Run count over time shown; Pipeline and task durations displayed; Performance trends identifiable
evidence: Metrics tab; Pipeline Success Ratio; Number of Pipeline Runs; Pipeline Run Duration; Task Run Duration
notes: Enables data-driven pipeline optimization

section: Interacting with pipelines using Developer perspective
job_statement: When my pipeline run fails, I want to access run details and logs quickly, so I can identify and debug the failure
prerequisites: Pipeline run exists; Pipeline Runs tab accessible
desired_outcomes: Failed run identified; Log snippet visible; Quick link to full logs available; Task run status clear
evidence: Pipeline Runs tab; Run status indicators; Log Snippet in Details section; Link to Logs section; Options menu for rerun
notes: Critical for debugging and failure resolution

job_statement: When I need to execute my pipeline, I want to start a pipeline run with specific resources and parameters, so I can run my CI/CD workflow on demand or test pipeline changes
prerequisites: Pipeline created; Git and image resources available or ready to create; Workspace volumes available
desired_outcomes: Pipeline run started; Resources selected or created; Parameters configured; Workspaces bound to volumes; Execution visible in PipelineRun details
evidence: Start Pipeline dialog; Git Resources and Image Resources fields; Parameters section; Workspaces section with volume source options; Advanced Options for credentials
notes: Primary execution entry point, supports on-demand and manual testing

job_statement: When my pipeline needs to access private Git repositories or registries, I want to add authentication secrets during pipeline start, so I can authorize access to protected resources
prerequisites: Pipeline start dialog open; Credentials for private Git or registry
desired_outcomes: Secret created with credentials; Authentication type configured; Provider and server URL specified; Secret available for pipeline run
evidence: Advanced Options -> Show Credentials Options; Create Source Secret section; Authentication types: Image Registry, Basic, SSH; Add Secret and Add Credentials buttons
notes: Enables pipelines to work with private resources securely

job_statement: When I start a pipeline run, I want to monitor task execution in real-time, so I can track progress and catch issues as they occur
prerequisites: Pipeline run started
desired_outcomes: Live task status visible; Step execution progress shown; Task durations displayed; Logs accessible per task; Events stream available
evidence: PipelineRun details visualization; Task status colors; Hover details for tasks; Logs tab with expandable pane; Events tab; Download logs options
notes: Real-time monitoring crucial for catching failures early

job_statement: When I am working with my application in Topology view, I want to start and monitor pipelines from the application context, so I can see my CI/CD status alongside my application deployment
prerequisites: Application created with From Git option; Pipeline associated with application
desired_outcomes: Pipeline run initiated from Topology; Pipeline status visible on application node; Start Last Run option available; Integrated view of app and pipeline
evidence: Topology view application node; Pipeline Runs side panel; Start Last Run button; Pipeline status icon; Resources tab with Log Snippet
notes: Application-centric workflow, integrates deployment and CI/CD views

section: Interacting with pipelines from Topology view
job_statement: When I am managing my application, I want to see pipeline status and failure details in the Topology view, so I can quickly understand build and deployment health without switching contexts
prerequisites: Application with pipeline in Topology view
desired_outcomes: Pipeline run status visible on app node; Not started pipelines identifiable; Failure log snippets accessible; Quick access to logs and details
evidence: Pipeline status icon on application; Not started status message; Log Snippet in Pipeline Runs section; Link to full logs; Builds section visibility
notes: Unified application and pipeline health monitoring

job_statement: When my pipeline requirements change, I want to edit existing pipelines, so I can add tasks, modify parameters, or update resources without recreating from scratch
prerequisites: Pipeline exists; Pipeline Details page access
desired_outcomes: Pipeline modified with new tasks or parameters; Task details updated; Tasks removed if needed; Changes saved and reflected in pipeline
evidence: Actions -> Edit Pipeline; Pipeline builder for editing; Task side panel for modifications; Actions -> Remove Task; Save button
notes: Iterative pipeline development and maintenance

job_statement: When pipelines are no longer needed, I want to delete them from the cluster, so I can clean up resources and maintain an organized pipeline inventory
prerequisites: Pipeline exists; Pipelines view access
desired_outcomes: Pipeline removed from cluster; Pipeline no longer appears in views; Confirmation prevents accidental deletion
evidence: Options menu -> Delete Pipeline; Delete Pipeline confirmation prompt; Delete button
notes: Lifecycle management for pipelines

section: Creating pipeline templates in Administrator perspective
job_statement: When I need to standardize pipelines across teams, I want to create reusable pipeline templates, so developers can quickly create pipelines following organizational best practices
prerequisites: Cluster administrator access; Administrator perspective; OpenShift Pipelines Operator installed
desired_outcomes: Template created in openshift namespace; Runtime and type labels applied; Template available to developers; Standardized pipeline patterns established
evidence: Import YAML flow; openshift namespace requirement; pipeline.openshift.io/runtime label; pipeline.openshift.io/type label; Pipeline details page
notes: Enables governance and standardization across development teams

section: Pipeline execution statistics in web console
job_statement: When I need to analyze pipeline performance and reliability, I want to view execution statistics and trends, so I can make informed decisions about pipeline improvements and capacity planning
prerequisites: Tekton Results installed; Pipelines console plugin enabled; Pipeline execution history
desired_outcomes: Statistics overview visible; Success rates and run counts displayed; Duration metrics available; Trends over time identifiable; Per-pipeline and aggregate views accessible
evidence: Pipelines -> Overview page; Pipeline details Metrics tab; Pipeline run graphs; Duration statistics (total, average, maximum); Pipeline table with duration and success rate
notes: Administrative observability for fleet-wide pipeline analysis

job_statement: When I want to access pipeline statistics, I want to enable the console plugin, so I can see execution metrics and performance data in the web console
prerequisites: Cluster administrator access; OpenShift 4.15 or later; Pipelines Operator installed
desired_outcomes: Console plugin enabled; Statistics features available; Plugin status shows Enabled
evidence: Operators -> Installed Operators; Console plugin status label; Enable option; Save button
notes: One-time configuration required for statistics features

job_statement: When I need to understand overall pipeline health, I want to view consolidated statistics across all pipelines, so I can assess system-wide CI/CD performance and identify problematic pipelines
prerequisites: Console plugin enabled; Tekton Results installed; Pipeline execution history
desired_outcomes: Aggregate metrics visible; Pipeline run status graph displayed; Duration metrics shown; Pipeline comparison table available; Time range and project filters applied
evidence: Pipelines -> Overview; Run status graph over time; Total/average/maximum duration; Pipeline table with all pipelines; Project, Time range, Refresh interval filters
notes: Fleet-wide observability for administrators and DevOps teams

section: Viewing statistics for a specific pipeline
job_statement: When I need to analyze a particular pipeline's performance, I want to view its execution statistics, so I can identify bottlenecks, success rates, and trends specific to that pipeline
prerequisites: Console plugin enabled; Pipeline with execution history; Pipelines page access
desired_outcomes: Pipeline-specific metrics displayed; Run status and count visible; Duration trends shown; Time-based filtering available
evidence: Pipeline details -> Metrics tab; Run status graph; Duration statistics; Time range and refresh interval controls
notes: Granular performance analysis for individual pipeline optimization
